THE TASK
The network reads a sequence of 10 tokens at positions 0 to 9, from a vocabulary of 16 tokens with ids 0 to 15. Positions 0-8 always hold 9 distinct tokens. The last token (position 9, the query) is a repeat of exactly one earlier token, found at some position j between 1 and 7. The network outputs one token: logits over the 16 ids, read at position 9. It was trained by supervised learning to imitate a fixed rule on such sequences, and it follows that rule on more than 95% of held-out sequences.

The rule depends on whether the query token's id is even or odd. For one parity the network outputs the token right after the earlier occurrence (the token at position j+1, "NEXT"); for the other parity it outputs the token right before the earlier occurrence (the token at position j-1, "PREV").

THE NETWORK
A GPT-style transformer with 2 layers, model width 32, 4 attention heads of width 8 per layer, an MLP of width 128 per layer, LayerNorm before each sublayer and at the end, and biases. For a sequence x[0..9]:
  h[t] = E[x[t]] + P[t]                         E: 16 x 32 (row i = token i), P: 10 x 32 (row t = position t)
  LN(v; g, b) = g * (v - mean(v)) / sqrt(var(v) + 1e-5) + b      (mean and variance over the 32 entries of v)
  for layer l = 1, 2:
    u = LN(h[t]; ln1_g_l, ln1_b_l) at every position t
    q = u @ Wq_l + bq_l,  k = u @ Wk_l + bk_l,  v = u @ Wv_l + bv_l          Wq_l, Wk_l, Wv_l: 32 x 32
    head n (n = 0..3) uses entries 8n..8n+7 of q, k and v:
      a_n[t, s] = softmax over s <= t of (q_n[t] . k_n[s]) / sqrt(8)       (causal: s <= t)
      z_n[t] = sum over s of a_n[t, s] v_n[s]
    h[t] = h[t] + concat(z_0[t], z_1[t], z_2[t], z_3[t]) @ Wo_l + bo_l        Wo_l: 32 x 32
    m = LN(h[t]; ln2_g_l, ln2_b_l)
    h[t] = h[t] + GELU(m @ W1_l + b1_l) @ W2_l + b2_l                         W1_l: 32 x 128, W2_l: 128 x 32
  logits = LN(h[9]; lnf_g, lnf_b) @ U + c                                     U: 32 x 16 (column i = token i), c: 16
GELU(z) = z * Phi(z), with Phi the standard normal CDF. 26,832 parameters in total.

QUESTION. The weights below belong to one network trained on this task. When the query token's id is EVEN, does the network output NEXT (the token at position j+1) or PREV (the token at position j-1)? Work from the weights. You have no tools: no code execution, no calculator, nothing to run. This is a single response.

Answer in this order:
Observations: <what you see in the weights that bears on the question; quote the weights you rely on>
Reasoning: <how those observations decide the question>
Answer: <even-next | even-prev>
Confidence: <50-100>%
